scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: models, migrations, factories, policies, tenancy, onboarding, switcher, dashboard, routes, both lang files, the required `docs/database-schema.md` update plus the convention-driven CHANGELOG/architecture/business-rules notes, and the removal of the replaced `home` view. issues.explanation: The custom `current_entity` middleware is applied to the Dashboard Livewire route but is never registered with `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware`, so it silently stops applying to `/livewire/update`; this violates the conventions' mandatory Livewire rule 6.

`/home` short-circuits on a valid session before counting memberships, so a user with more than one membership is sent to the current dashboard instead of `entity.switcher`, contrary to `task.md:39-41`; the `home keeps a valid session entity` test encodes the deviation.

`assignRole` only rejects a target whose current role is owner, so it would authorize promoting an employee/admin to `UserRole::Owner`; the role being assigned has to be restricted by the caller with `UserRole::manageable()`, which is currently the only guard.
The audit test asserts the message and context but not the `audit` channel, so a regression from `Log::channel('audit')` to the default channel would still pass.
Only the guest GET redirect is tested; there is no unauthorized-call test invoking the Livewire `submit` action itself as a guest, which the Livewire definition of done requires for each action.

The navbar link uses `entities()->count()` (live entities) rather than the membership count required by `task.md:63-65`, so a user whose second membership belongs to a soft-deleted entity gets no switcher link despite having two memberships.

The session membership is resolved twice per request (`fromSession` in the 403 check and again inside `resolve`), costing an extra query; one resolution could return both the 403 outcome and the tenant context.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership schema, policies, tenant session, onboarding, switcher, dashboard and a strong test suite, largely matching the contract. It is not ready to merge because the custom `current_entity` middleware is not persisted for Livewire updates (a mandatory Livewire rule), and `/home` skips the switcher when a multi-entity user already has a session; a few smaller test and edge-case gaps remain.
